long_biography.plain_text:
When Anthony Ward left Phibro in 1998, he carried its cocoa staff and contracts into Armajaro, financed by two banks and capital he raised with Richard Gower. The arrangement converted his commodity-market experience into an enterprise trading physical cocoa and coffee, derivatives and, later, investment funds.

Ward pushed Armajaro towards traceable supply chains in Ghana as buyers became more concerned about cocoa's origins. He then separated physical supply from a hedge fund so that his trading did not conflict with customers. The physical commodities division was sold to Ecom, and Ward ultimately closed his cocoa fund as algorithmic trading weakened the advantage of fundamental market research.
